name: Muricy Ramalho
scopeNote: Narrowed on 2026-11-04: only São Paulo 2006-09 is counted; the Fluminense 2010-11 and Santos 2011-13 spells are excluded and their sources stay in the file as context with verified false. Spells proposed by the researcher under the catalog policy (tier A/B tactical coverage plus titles): Sao Paulo 2006-01-03 to 2009-06-19 (Brasileirao 2006, 2007, 2008), Fluminense 2010-04-25 to 2011-03-13 (Brasileirao 2010), Santos 2011-04-05 to 2013-05-31 (Libertadores 2011, Paulista 2011 and 2012, Recopa 2012). The 2011 Libertadores and the work with Neymar/Ganso are the Santos core; the Santos spell is counted whole because the end date is the one given by Wikipedia (dismissal 31 May 2013). Dates come from English Wikipedia (start 3 Jan 2006, 19 Jun 2009 firing confirmed by Jornal de Brasilia same day, 25 Apr 2010, 13 Mar 2011 confirmed by Fox Sports 14 Mar 2011, 5-6 Apr 2011, 31 May 2013). Brazilian tactical coverage is thin: almost no tier A source exists; most evidence is tier C press and Trivela (tier B). The popular label for his Sao Paulo is 'tricampeao com tres zagueiros / 3-5-2' (Correio Braziliense blog, 2021, retrospective), but the only starting XI found for a title game (2006) lists four defenders in a 4-4-2 on paper and Trivela 2008 says he had not decided between three or four centre-backs, so the 3-5-2 label is not uniform across 2006-08. At Santos 2011 the source (DOL) says the midfield marked 'por setor' with a new positioning, i.e. zonal in midfield; no source states man-marking versus zonal for the whole team. A 4-4-2 with a flat midfield is documented for Sao Paulo 2014 (Trivela) and Flamengo 2016 (Lance), both outside the counted spells, and as a Muricy view in 2020 (Netflu); it is not documented for 2006-08 or Fluminense 2010. Pressing in the modern sense is not documented for the counted spells: the sources describe a compact, obedient, counter-attacking side. Partial dates in spellsExcluded (Internacional 2004-2005, Sao Paulo 1994-1996) come from Wikipedia's career table, which gives no day; they are excluded spells so no exact date was pursued. Possession is not documented for any counted spell (only the 2019 stated view that having the ball reduces risk). Fluminense 2010 (Trivela 2011-02-23, Lance retrospective) is described as organised, defensive and counter-attacking; the Lance article is a recent retrospective with a narrative tone, use with caution.
openQuestions: Shape 2006-08: Correio Braziliense (2021 blog) says the Sao Paulo of 2006-08 played with three centre-backs; the 2006 title-game line-up (Gazeta SP retrospective) shows four defenders and a 4-4-2 on paper (Ilsinho, Fabao, Miranda, Junior; Josue, Mineiro, Souza, Danilo; Leandro, Aloisio); Trivela 2008 says Muricy had not decided between three and four. A tier A/B match-level source would settle it.

Fluminense 2010: Trivela summaries seen in a search result (switch from three to two centre-backs late in the second half of the season) were not confirmed on a readable page; no verified shape fact for Fluminense.

Zonal versus man-marking: Jornal de Brasilia 2006-05-18 says Muricy considered moving from individual to zonal marking against aerial balls; whether he did is not confirmed. Santos 2011 (DOL) says midfield marked por setor. No source for 2007-08.
Wikipedia cites a 2008 blog 'Sao Paulo's Sweeney Todd: How Muricy Ramalho is killing the game' (pitacodogringo) as criticism of his methods; not read.
Excluded spells have not been checked for dates beyond what the Wikipedia infobox/search summaries say.

spellsCounted.reason: Three consecutive Brasileirao titles (2006, 2007, 2008), best defence in the points-based era in 2007, Libertadores 2006 final; most documented spell.

spellsExcluded.reason: Runner-up in the 2005 Brasileirao; no tier A/B tactical coverage found; exact dates not verified (Wikipedia lists 2003 and 2004-2005 spells).
No title, sacked after a 1-4 defeat to Sao Caetano; thin tactical coverage; dates from Wikipedia.
No title (runner-up 2014); Trivela 4-4-2 analysis exists (2014-08-21) but the policy keeps the signature spells; ended for health reasons.
Five months, no title, left after hospitalisation for arrhythmia; Lance documents a 4-4-2 trial in April 2016; end date from a search summary, not verified.
Copa CONMEBOL 1994 with a youth/reserve team; outside the modern era, no tactical coverage.

sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spell (São Paulo 2006-09), kept as context] Sem contar as quatro primeiras rodadas, quando os jogadores ainda se adaptavam ao estilo do técnico Muricy Ramalho, que assumiu o cargo no final de abril, a equipe sempre esteve entre os três primeiros colocados da competição.

statedView.quote: Não gosto de pôr muita pilha porque, às vezes, isso faz mal ao jogador. Quando ele entra muito aceso, esquece a tática e a técnica.
A defesa não começa lá atrás. Começa na frente. É muito legal o futebol do Santos, mas tem que saber que sem a bola tem que trabalhar um pouquinho.
Eu queria ter mais uns cinco problemáticos como ele. São jogadores como Neymar que fazem a diferença.
Foi um tricampeonato de um técnico em um único time, e isso é inédito.
Only when they win trophies here [Brazil] they will be the best coaches in the world.
Hoje você tem o controle de jogo, a famosa posse de bola. E a intensidade. Futebol hoje faz a transição rápida
Quando você tem a posse de bola você corre menos riscos.

Jogador é folgado, se acomoda fácil. Ele ganha um jogo e acha que ganhou a Copa do Mundo, então você tem que estar colocando ele sempre com o pezinho no chão. [...] A minha maior briga no São Paulo não era nem tático, nem técnico, nem físico. Era mentalmente

influences: Barcelona stage (2015) as a late influence on his stated view of possession and fast transition; no influence documented for 2006-13

confidence.reason: Titles and dates are solid, but no tier A source exists and tier B (Trivela) covers only Fluminense 2010, the 2008 start and later spells; most tactical evidence is tier C press or retrospectives. Shape for 2006-08 is contradictory (3-5-2 label versus a 4-4-2 line-up sheet), the Fluminense and 2006 shapes come from match sheets, and possession is undocumented.
